primary.title: The Origin and Progress of the Mechanical Inventions of James Watt
primary.author: James Watt
primary.rationale: This is a collection of Watt's own writings, patents, and correspondence, offering direct insight into his inventions and thoughts. It was compiled posthumously but contains his original work.

primary.title: Correspondence of James Watt and Matthew Boulton
primary.author: James Watt
primary.rationale: This collection of letters between James Watt and his business partner Matthew Boulton provides a detailed account of their collaboration, business dealings, and the development of the steam engine.

secondary.title: James Watt: The Birth of the Modern World
secondary.author: David Philip Miller
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive biography by a respected historian, published by a major academic press, offering a modern scholarly assessment of Watt's life and impact.

secondary.title: James Watt: His Life and Inventions
secondary.author: Andrew Carnegie
secondary.rationale: While older, Carnegie's work is a significant historical account, often drawing on primary sources. It's a foundational text for understanding Watt, and its availability on platforms like Project Gutenberg makes it accessible for research.

secondary.title: The Steam Engine of Watt
secondary.author: J. G. R. Ellis
secondary.rationale: This article likely provides a focused scholarly analysis of Watt's most significant invention, offering technical and historical context.

suggestions.notes: Finding extensive primary source texts *authored by* James Watt and readily available on Wikisource or Project Gutenberg is challenging. Collections of his correspondence and writings are more likely found on Internet Archive. The secondary sources prioritize recent scholarly works and a foundational, widely accessible older biography.
